title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། ཆེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 175)
shelf_note: Authentic volume of the Pramāṇa (epistemology and logic) section of the Derge Tengyur.

tr_errors_B.english: If seeing occurs without distinction regarding the essence of the thing as separate from everything else, why is there certainty regarding the aspects experienced as they truly are?
tr_errors_B.problem: The text ends mid-sentence at the bottom of the folio, but Translation B invents a closed question that reverses the sense of the objection (asking why certainty exists rather than why ascertainment fails to arise).

tr_errors_B.english: <note>This refers to the Buddhist logical theory where perceiving an object should theoretically mean perceiving all its qualities, yet conceptual thought must still work to eliminate false impositions.</note>
tr_errors_B.problem: Invented explanatory commentary note not present in the Tibetan source text.

pages.prefer_reason: Translation A accurately captures the technical Pramāṇa terminology, preserves the dialectical structure and the trailing sentence fragment at the bottom of the folio, and avoids inserting invented commentary.

book_verdict: An authentic Derge Tengyur Pramāṇa woodblock folio with flawless transcription, where Translation A provides a highly faithful rendering.
